text:
Predicates:
Listed(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
NegativeReviews(x) ::: x has received many negative reviews.
RatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ProvidesTakeout(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
Popular(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Premises:
∀x (Listed(x) → ¬NegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then the restaurant has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (RatingGreaterThanFour(x) → Listed(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeout(x) ∧ NegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (Popular(x) → RatingGreaterThanFour(x)) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
RatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenPlazaSubway) ∨ Popular(hamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.
Conclusion:
(ProvidesTakeout(hamdenPlazaSubway) ∧ NegativeReviews(hamdenPlazaSubway)) → (RatingGreaterThanFour(hamdenPlazaSubway) ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeout(hamdenPlazaSubway)) ::: If the Hamden Plaza Subway store provides take-out service and receives many negative reviews, then its rating is greater than 4 and it does not provide take-out service.
